gbm_population_evidence.quote: Participants must have histologically or cytologically confirmed WHO grade 4 glioma (including tumors with molecularly defined grade 4 astrocytoma)

candidate_evidence.quote: While sitagliptin is FDA-approved for diabetes treatment, its use in glioblastoma is investigational (experimental).

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: A Phase 2 and Pharmacodynamic Study of Sitagliptin in Patients With Progressive Grade 4 Gliomas

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: Difference in tumor CD8+ T cell count between the participants randomized to pre-surgical sitagliptin versus the participants randomized to no pre-surgical treatment.
Investigators hypothesize that treating GBM patients with sitagliptin will deplete circulating MDSCs and reduce their entry into the brain

role_evidence.quote: Sitagliptin is an investigational drug for this condition that works by inhibiting an enzyme called dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4)

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: Inhibits DPP-4 to deplete circulating MDSCs and reduce their entry into the brain, reversing immunosuppression
arms: Group 1: Presurgical and post surgical treatment with sitagliptin:
Group 2: Post surgical treatment with sitagliptin:

coder_notes: Post-operative 'chemotherapy' is unnamed and not a registered intervention, so not listed as an agent; regimen coded combination because all patients receive chemotherapy with sitagliptin. Group 2 (no presurgical sitagliptin) serves as the comparison for the primary outcome though both arms are labelled EXPERIMENTAL. Eligibility is WHO grade 4 glioma including molecularly defined grade 4 astrocytoma (may include IDH-mutant); GBM named in conditions.
